name: Player List Item
desc: Adds, updates, or removes entries from the tab player list. Used for player join/leave, gamemode changes, ping updates, and display name changes.

fields.name: players
fields.desc: List of AddPlayerData entries (UUID, name, profile properties, gamemode, ping, display name)

encoding: UUID + String + Property[] + VarInt + VarInt + ChatComponent
notes: Action 0 (ADD_PLAYER): UUID, name, skin properties, gamemode, ping, display name. Action 4 (REMOVE_PLAYER): just UUID. Action 2 (UPDATE_LATENCY): UUID + ping. This is how the client builds the tab list and gets player skins.

writeup.p: The tab list state machine: one VarInt action plus a list of per-player records. ADD_PLAYER (0) ships UUID, name, the skin property map, gamemode, ping and an optional display name; UPDATE_GAME_MODE (1) and UPDATE_LATENCY (2) carry a UUID plus one field; UPDATE_DISPLAY_NAME (3) a UUID plus an optional chat component; REMOVE_PLAYER (4) a bare UUID. ServerConfigurationManager broadcasts ADD on join, REMOVE on leave, and every 600 ticks it broadcasts UPDATE_LATENCY for the whole list, which is how ping reaches the tab GUI.

handlePlayerListItem branches per action and mutates the player info map: ADD builds a NetworkPlayerInfo from the AddPlayerData, UPDATE_LATENCY overwrites the ping field, UPDATE_DISPLAY_NAME swaps the display name, REMOVE drops the entry. The ADD path doubles as the skin pipeline: the textures property is consumed by the player renderer. Server side, the packet constructors snapshot each EntityPlayerMP's profile, ping, gamemode and tab display name into records.

Four modules across three clients. Rise 5.99 Denicker intercepts ADD_PLAYER, decodes the base64 textures property from the GameProfile and compares the embedded profileName against the displayed name to reveal nicked players, pairing results with S02PacketChat join lines. Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 StaffDetector keep a hardcoded staff list, but the S38 handler is commented out in both builds, leaving only the PreMotion decay counter live. Sigma 4.11 AntiVanish reads UPDATE_LATENCY and REMOVE_PLAYER to catch vanished players, and FriendAlert notifies when an ADD_PLAYER name matches the friend list.

The ADD_PLAYER payload is the richest unencrypted metadata stream in the protocol: the full GameProfile including signed skin properties, which Denicker turns into an identity oracle that nick plugins do not scrub. UPDATE_LATENCY is a ping heartbeat that enables vanish detection: a vanished player stops appearing, and AntiVanish also flags latency updates for UUIDs absent from the player info map. No anti-cheat polices the packet; the countermeasures are tab-list plugins that strip or re-sign properties.

implementation.overview: The tab list state machine and the most information-dense clientbound metadata channel: ADD_PLAYER carries full GameProfiles with signed skin properties. Four corpus modules live on it: Rise 5.99 Denicker decodes skin payloads to un-nick players, Rise 6.x StaffDetector carries a disabled S38 hook, and Sigma 4.11 AntiVanish and FriendAlert track the latency heartbeat and join records.
implementation.server_handling: ServerConfigurationManager sends ADD to everyone when a player joins and REMOVE on quit; the joining player additionally receives ADD records for everyone already online. onTick broadcasts UPDATE_LATENCY for the whole list every 600 ticks. The channel is broadcast-only: the server never validates what the client does with the data, and there is no clientbound acknowledgment.
implementation.protocol_notes: The action is a VarInt enum. Record layout depends on action; the widest is ADD_PLAYER: UUID, name capped at 16 chars, VarInt property count, then per property name, value and optional signature strings with a boolean flag, then gamemode VarInt, ping VarInt and an optional chat component. Property strings cap at 32767 bytes. UPDATE_LATENCY entries are only UUID plus ping VarInt, which is why ping refreshes stay cheap.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Not a detection surface; no anti-cheat measures tab list traffic. The realistic risks are social and structural: Denicker's un-nicking fails when servers strip profileName from the textures payload, and vanish alerts are defeated by networks that keep vanished players in the tab list, which is exactly why Sigma hard-disables AntiVanish on hypixel, hive and mineplex via a server-IP check.

modules.name: Denicker
modules.purpose: Reveal the real identity of nicked players by decoding the signed skin texture payload from ADD_PLAYER records.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketReceiveEvent, an ADD_PLAYER S38 is read: the first AddPlayerData's GameProfile is taken, the textures property is base64-decoded into JSON, and the embedded profileName is compared with the displayed name. Mismatches are queued as realName=nickedName pairs; S02PacketChat join messages are then scanned on a background thread, and a matching nick triggers a notification plus a log4j chat rewrite when overlay support is on.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: No anti-cheat involvement; the countermeasure is server-side property scrubbing. Servers that strip or re-sign the textures property defeat the decode, which is why the module only works on networks that leave profileName intact.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 only; no other corpus client ships an S38-based denicker.

modules.name: StaffDetector
modules.purpose: Detect staff on the server by matching tab list names against a hardcoded staff list, then auto-leave via /hub.
modules.how_it_works: The module keeps a hardcoded comma-separated staff name list and a PreMotion counter that decays each tick. In both corpus builds the actual packet handling is commented out: the S38 ADD_PLAYER and S3EPacketTeams branches that would count staff sightings and send /hub at count 6 are dead code. Only the name list and the decay counter remain live.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: No anti-cheat risk; the feature is a reconnaissance countermeasure. The hardcoded list is per-network and rots quickly, which is presumably why the hook was disabled in the shipped builds.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 carries the same file under com/alan/clients/module/impl/exploit with the same commented-out S38 branch.

modules.name: AntiVanish
modules.purpose: Detect vanished players by watching UPDATE_LATENCY and REMOVE_PLAYER records that reference UUIDs absent from the tab list.
modules.how_it_works: On EventPacket (incoming), UPDATE_LATENCY records are checked against mc.getNetHandler().getPlayerInfo(uuid): a latency update for a UUID with no player info entry is flagged as a vanished player and added to a watch list. On the update event, any watched UUID that later gains a player info entry is reported as un-vanished. A REMOVE_PLAYER branch prints the removed display name. A server-IP guard auto-disables on hypixel, hive and mineplex.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: No anti-cheat risk; the module is pure tab list observation. Its practical weakness is structural: any server that keeps vanished players listed (Hypixel-style) defeats the oracle, which is why the module refuses to run there.
modules.variations: Sigma-only. Rise 6.x attempts the inverse (staff detection) with a name list; no other client watches the latency heartbeat.

modules.name: FriendAlert
modules.purpose: Notify when a friend joins by matching ADD_PLAYER profile names against the friend manager.
modules.how_it_works: On incoming EventPacket, an ADD_PLAYER S38 is iterated and each AddPlayerData's profile name is checked with FriendManager.isFriend; a match posts a Friend Alert notification with the name. The module reads only the name field and ignores the skin properties.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: No detection surface; join alerts are indistinguishable from passive tab list rendering to the server.
modules.variations: Sigma-only in the corpus; Rise 5.99's Denicker pairs ADD_PLAYER with S02 join messages instead of relying on the friend manager.

implementation.general_hooks: PacketReceiveEvent / incoming EventPacket is universal; Rise 6.x adds its component system on top of the same receive bus.
implementation.client_variations: Sigma reads fields through the MCP accessors (func_179768_b, func_179767_a, field_179964_d); Rise 5.99 uses the same MCP names; Rise 6.x uses renamed accessors (getMatches-style). None of the four modules mutate the packet; all are read-only consumers.

anticheat.overview: The player-list packet manages tab list entries: add, remove, and updates of game mode, ping and display name. Server-side anticheats almost never validate it, and in this corpus only Grim consumes it: one listener rewrites game modes to hide spectators, and the entity replication listener stores the UUID-to-profile mappings that checks use to resolve entity identities. The keyword noise in the corpus is tab-complete and math-table code, not player-list handling.

checks.name: Spectator hiding in the player list (Grim)
checks.purpose: Prevent spectators on Grim's spectate system from leaking through the tab list with spectator game mode.
checks.how_it_works: PacketHidePlayerInfo is a HIGHEST-priority send listener. For PLAYER_INFO (pre-1.19.3) it walks the player data list and, for entries that should be hidden, rewrites SPECTATOR game mode to SURVIVAL, cancels the packet when every entry was hidden and the action was a pure game-mode update, and marks the packet for re-encoding otherwise. The 1.19.3+ PLAYER_INFO_UPDATE path does the same per entry, removes the UPDATE_GAME_MODE action from a cancelled packet, and re-encodes modified entries.
checks.detects: Not a cheat detection: it hides the anticheat's own spectators from other players' tab lists, which also removes the game-mode tell that would expose staff spectating.
checks.variations: No other anticheat in the corpus touches player-list packets; the rest of the S38 corpus hits are tab-complete (C0B) or table-name keyword noise.

checks.name: Player-list replication (Grim)
checks.purpose: Record the UUID-to-profile mappings announced on the player list so entity and profile lookups in checks resolve correctly.
checks.how_it_works: PacketEntityReplication wraps PLAYER_INFO and PLAYER_INFO_UPDATE sends and, transaction-sandwiched, puts ADD_PLAYER game profiles into compensatedEntities.profiles and removes them on REMOVE_PLAYER. The profile map feeds checks that need the game profile behind an entity id or uuid.
checks.detects: None directly; it is state replication that keeps the compensated entity model consistent with the tab list.
checks.variations: No other anticheat in the corpus reads player-list packets; Grim's SpectateManager is the only consumer of the stored profiles besides the checks themselves.
